## The Core Claim

Real, human choices systematically and predictably violate expected-utility theory's independence axiom (the Allais paradox, 1953) in a specific direction driven by loss aversion -- a reference-dependent value function, steeper for losses than equivalent gains, formalized as Prospect Theory (Kahneman & Tversky, 1979). This is not noise around the rational-choice model; it is a structured, predictable departure from it, awarded the 2002 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for integrating psychological insight into economic science.
